usual_baseline: Diagnosis within 48 hours is near-universal (97–100%). Severity scoring is poor: 6–38% documented. Ultrasound within 24 hours 25–41%. Cause identified in 55–82%, with up to 46% labelled idiopathic. Inappropriate antibiotics in 42% and 22 of 56. Index-admission or two-week cholecystectomy as low as 7.1–18%.
fix_that_works: A weekly benign upper GI MDT with ERCP and hot cholecystectomy pathways: two-week cholecystectomy 75% to 100%, imaging within 24 hours 100%, escalation 0% to 60% [2602]. Extra hot chole slots: early cholecystectomy 18% to 31%, inappropriate antibiotics 42% to 28% [2704]. Teaching and MDT posters: aetiology 62% to 100%, risk stratification 38% to 65% [2881].
fix_that_fails: Risk stratification stayed below standard after teaching, at 65% [2881], and Glasgow score within 48 hours reached only 50% [2602]. Early cholecystectomy still only 31% after extra theatre slots [2704]. Most projects planned bundles, proformas or pathways but reported no re-audit [2084, 2471, 2572, 2879, 2880].
consultant_advice: Heavily audited, and most projects never close the loop. Pick one measure, such as Glasgow-Imrie scoring at 48 hours or cholecystectomy within two weeks for gallstone cases, and re-audit it. Fluid volumes, nutrition and antibiotic indication are rarely measured and are worth doing.
